cert.note.cegis: The list of counterexamples IS the certificate: it is the minimal set of inputs that pins this solution down.
cert.note.cnf_model: Checked clause by clause. No solver, no propagation.
cert.note.drat: Refutation proof. Checked by unit propagation (RUP/RAT): no SAT solver is involved, so the one that produced it need not be trusted.
cert.note.shrink_graph: Minimal (1-minimal), not minimum. `blocked` is the witness: every one-step reduction either fails a filter or satisfies the predicate. Verifying requires the spec module, whose hash is included.
cert.note.mus: Minimal unsatisfiable subset. The DRAT proof refutes the MUS and each witness is a model of the MUS without one of its clauses: together they certify unsatisfiability AND minimality without a solver.
cert.note.bisect: The threshold is certified by the pair that brackets it: a proof on the good side and a refutation on the bad side. Each is verified separately. MONOTONICITY in t is assumed, not proved.
cert.note.synth_proved: Two chained obligations: the bounded synthesis that found the candidate and the universal symbolic proof of it. Each is verified separately; the one that counts as a theorem is the second.
cert.note.sweep: Two different things: which family was examined (verifiable here) and whether the predicate was evaluated correctly on each graph (only if the predicate supplied a certificate: {certified} of {total} entries). COMPLETENESS of the family requires re-enumerating.
cert.note.graph_set: Verifies pairwise non-isomorphism and the filters. COMPLETENESS (that none is missing) can only be checked by re-enumerating.

A tree with a missing child reads exactly like a complete one.

lint.spec.magnitude: this claim divides by a product of symbols ({names}). If the question is whether it DECAYS in a growth parameter, `prove` cannot answer it -- a term that is Theta(1) is satisfiable forever and never improves. `certo order` reports the exponent, with a certificate.
lint.spec.high_degree: the claim is a univariate polynomial of degree {degree}. `prove` proves degree {proved} in milliseconds and times out at degree {cliff}, measured on a statement that is trivially true -- so expect no certificate. A substitution that lowers the degree (t = s^3 for a claim written in t^3) usually turns it back into one certo closes at once.

It does NOT say the solution is non-negative, and over the rationals it does not say it is integral -- a rational solution to the equations of a packing is not a packing. equitable.double_count: the double count fails at ({i}, {j}): N.H = {lhs} but M.B = {rhs}, in {n} pair(s). Both regularities were established, so this is an internal inconsistency rather than a bad partition

cert.note.equitable_quotient: an equivalence between two programs, not an agreement between two computed optima
verify.quotient.double_count: the two regularities cohere: N_i H_ij = M_j B_ij
verify.quotient.rebuilt: the quotient is the one the class data produces
verify.quotient.roundtrip: lifting then projecting is the identity
verify.quotient.method: by redoing the double count and rebuilding the quotient from the class data: no solver, and the regularity against the physical matrix was established when the certificate was produced
verify.quotient.detail: {prows}x{pcols} and {rows}x{cols} have the same attainable values
verify.quotient.scope: this is an EQUIVALENCE of the two programs, not a claim about what their common optimum is. Solve either with `opt`. That the partition is the one your problem has -- the right classes, the right capacities -- is the spec's claim, and it is checked against the matrix rather than assumed, which is why a class mixing two capacities is refused.
verify.quotient.integrality: it says NOTHING about integrality. The equivalence is between the FRACTIONAL programs: an integer orbit mass need not lift to integer objects, and on K4 with triangles only the fractional programs agree while the integer packing is strictly smaller. A quotient certificate is never evidence about an integer program.

The multipliers and the square hints are in the certificate and can be transcribed.

semigroup.not_integer: `{name}` has a coordinate that is not an integer
semigroup.no_generators: a semigroup needs at least one generator
semigroup.mixed_dimension: the generators have different numbers of coordinates: {got}
semigroup.unknown_generator: `order` names generators that do not exist: {names}
semigroup.point_dimension: `{name}` has {got} coordinates and the generators have {want}

engine.semigroup.not_pointed: no grading found, so no search here terminates: the semigroup may not be pointed
engine.semigroup.not_pointed_proved: not pointed, proved: the combination ({witness}) of the generators is zero, so no search here terminates

engine.semigroup.redundant: {n} generator(s) lie in the semigroup generated by the others

verify.semigroup.pointed_undecided: none found, and the certificate leaves pointedness undecided

verify.semigroup.grading_is: u = ({values}), pairing at least 1 on every generator
verify.semigroup.cone_absence: a point outside the cone with no separator is outside by an exhaustive search, rerun
verify.semigroup.witness: each refutation has all three parts

verify.semigroup.detail: {n} generators in dimension {dim}, rank {rank}, {witnesses} normality witness(es)

verify.semigroup.summaries: every summary, recomputed from its parts
verify.semigroup.hilbert: the proposed minimal generating set, decided again
engine.semigroup.hilbert_yes: the proposed set IS the minimal generating set
engine.semigroup.hilbert_no: the proposed set is NOT the minimal generating set: {why}
engine.semigroup.hilbert_unknown: the proposed set could not be decided
cli.semigroup.unreachable: not reachable from the proposed set: {names}
verify.bad_dict: this looks like a serialised certificate but could not be read as one: {message}

cli.tamper.header: forging a `{kind}` certificate, one field at a time
cli.tamper.means: an uncaught field either carries no claim -- and does not belong in a payload that claims to be checkable -- or carries one and nothing is checking it. Only you can tell which
cli.tamper.unshaped: not probed, nothing of the same shape to put there: {names}
cli.tamper.excused: {n} field(s) excused as descriptive for this kind; --tamper-all probes them too
cli.tamper.original_fails: this certificate does not verify, so forging it proves nothing: every mutation would be caught by the failure already there. {detail}
profile.no_columns: a profile needs at least one column
profile.no_parameter: name the row whose capacity is the parameter
profile.parameter_has_capacity: `{row}` is the parameter, so `t` is its capacity: giving it a fixed one would be a second, silent answer
profile.no_segments: a profile needs at least one segment
profile.no_sources: a profile needs a source at every breakpoint
profile.empty_segment: segment {i} runs from {a} to {b}, which is empty
engine.profile.fails: the proposed profile does NOT hold: {why}
cert.note.capacity_profile: A function, certified: how an optimum responds to one capacity, on a whole interval. Bound plus attainment plus coverage is equality.
commands.q.profile: how does the optimum respond as ONE capacity goes from lo to hi -- the whole function, not one value?
verify.profile.dual: every dual is non-negative and covers every column
verify.profile.sources: every source is feasible at its own capacity
verify.profile.meet: bound and attainment MEET at every breakpoint
verify.profile.equality: this is what turns two inequalities into a value
verify.profile.stated: the stated piecewise form is the one the duals give
verify.profile.scope: This decides f on its domain FOR THIS COLUMN SET. It does not establish that the columns are all the columns, nor that the rows mean what they are called -- if they came from a graph, that translation is a separate obligation.
verify.profile.method: exact rational arithmetic; duals, sources, segment values and coverage all recomputed from the columns
verify.profile.derived: {n} breakpoint(s) and every source filed under its own capacity
engine.opt.empty_program: an empty program: no variables and no rows. Its optimum is the empty sum, zero, and a certificate of that establishes nothing -- so none is written
profile.budget: the search solved {n} programs without finishing; a profile is not reported as shorter than it is
profile.too_deep: the refinement nested deeper than any real profile does; stopping rather than guessing
profile.no_source_found: no primal could be rebuilt at t = {t} from that point's own dual
engine.profile.found: profile FOUND and certified: {n} segment(s) from {s} linear program(s)
doctor.what.clarabel: sos: the interior-point SDP solve that finds most sum-of-squares certificates
doctor.without.clarabel: `sos` falls back to alternating projections, which certified 6 of 30 random sums of squares where Clarabel certified 26; pip install 'certo[numerics]'
doctor.what.highs: opt: HiGHS in-process for every continuous solve -- an LP, or the relaxation of an ILP
doctor.without.highs: `opt` solves LPs with CBC instead, which starts a subprocess each time: 258 ms against 1.3 on the same small LP; pip install 'certo[numerics]'
doctor.what.cddlib: semigroup: the facets of the cone, which decide pointedness, cone membership and the separator instead of searching subsets
doctor.without.cddlib: `semigroup` searches subsets of generators instead: measured, it found a grading for 77 of 140 pointed cones where the facets found all 140; pip install 'certo[polyhedra]' (on Linux and macOS it builds against cddlib and GMP, e.g. apt install libcdd-dev libgmp-dev)
commands.q.report: is this certo's bug, my spec's, or my machine's -- and how do I report it?
cli.report.spec_warning: !! it includes YOUR SPEC, which may be unpublished mathematics. Read the folder before sharing it
cli.report.coverage_included: the coverage summary is included: counts and sizes only
cli.report.private: a certificate that verifies and is false is reported PRIVATELY: {link}
cli.report.nothing_sent: nothing has been sent -- what you share is your decision
cli.report.captured: A report was written for you, and nothing was sent: {path}

lean.lp.not_exact: only an EXACT LP certificate goes to Lean: a floating-point dual is not a proof there either
lean.lp.too_large: {hyps} hypotheses over {vars} variables: past {limit}, that `linarith` closes it in reasonable time is not a promise worth making
engine.opt.direction_unknown: --dual-direction names constraints the program does not have: {names} (it has {known})
verify.lp.dual_selection: the dual is the one maximising the stated direction among the optimal duals
verify.lp.dual_selection_is: second LP rebuilt from this certificate and verified; d.y = {value}
spec.cite_no_source: cited lemma `{name}` needs a `source`: where the statement comes from is the whole of what stands behind it
engine.compose.relative: RELATIVE to {n} cited lemma(s) certo did not check: {names}
verify.proof.cited_shape: cited lemma `{name}` is declared as cited, with a source and no certificate
verify.proof.cited: `{name}` is CITED, not checked, and the final step uses it: the theorem holds relative to it. Source: {source}. Statement: {statement}
verify.proof.cited_unused: `{name}` is cited ({source}) but the final step does not use it: the theorem does not rest on it
packing.map.partial: a map needs all three of graph=, cliques= and edges=: half a map checks half a translation and says nothing about the rest
packing.map.refused: the rows are not the graph's ({n} problem(s)): {problems}
packing.map.bad_edge: edge {edge} is not a pair of distinct vertices
packing.map.edge_twice: edge {edge} is listed twice in the graph
packing.map.not_an_edge: resource `{resource}` is said to be edge {edge}, which the graph does not have
packing.map.edge_reused: resources `{other}` and `{resource}` are both edge {edge}: one edge, two capacities
packing.map.resource_unmapped: resource `{resource}` is used by an item and is no declared edge
packing.map.item_unmapped: item `{item}` is not said to be any clique
packing.map.clique_without_item: `{item}` is declared as a clique but is no item of the packing
packing.map.clique_twice: items `{other}` and `{item}` are the same clique ({clique})
packing.map.not_a_clique: item `{item}` is not a clique: missing edge(s) {missing}
packing.map.edge_without_row: item `{item}`'s clique uses edge(s) {edges} that no resource row accounts for
packing.map.resource_twice: item `{item}` uses the same resource twice
packing.map.extra_resource: item `{item}` uses resource(s) {resources} that are not edges of its clique

packing.map.row_unmapped: row `{row}` is neither a declared edge nor a load
packing.map.coefficient: row `{row}` has coefficient {value} on `{item}`: a clique uses an edge once
packing.map.malformed: the map in the certificate is malformed

verify.lp.map_detail: {items} cliques over {rows} edge rows, against a graph of {edges} edges
verify.lp.map_scope: the MAP is checked -- rows against edges, columns against cliques. Which cliques should be in the family, and the capacities, are the spec's and are not

verify.proof.assumptions_named: every hypothesis entering the final step is named, once
packing.map.outside_unknown: `{name}` is declared outside the map but is no item or resource of the packing
packing.map.both: `{name}` is declared both in the map and outside it
verify.lp.map_outside: {items} item(s) declared no clique and {rows} row(s) declared no edge are OUTSIDE the map: nothing checks what they are

outcome.partition.failed: the predicate's partition is not an exact clique partition, so this item is undecided, not refuted: {detail}
outcome.partition.too_many: the predicate's partition uses {size} cliques, more than {at_most}: undecided, not refuted -- another partition might do
outcome.partition.ok: an exact clique partition into {size}{bound} cliques, certified by cover

verify.sweep.entry_subject_detail: {n} cover(s) compared with the graph their entry names; wrong: {names}

verify.colgen.farkas_pricing: no allowed clique has a positive sum of the vector over its edges (search rerun)
verify.colgen.detail_infeasible: the {problem} over every allowed clique of a graph on {n} vertices and {m} edges is INFEASIBLE
atlas.box_missing: a box gives no interval for `{name}`
atlas.domain_bounded: the domain must be a bounded box: every parameter an interval [lo, hi] with lo < hi
atlas.wrong_ring: the pieces are in parameters ({got}), the domain in ({want}): the same ring, in the same order
atlas.piece_failed: piece {k} did not certify, so it covers nothing: {detail}
atlas.no_pieces: an atlas needs pieces: parametric certificates, paths to them, or ParametricSpecs
atlas.no_parametric: no piece is a parametric_bound certificate
atlas.no_claim: an atlas makes ONE statement, so it needs a claim: give `claim=`, or pieces certified with one
atlas.cite_no_source: a cited box needs a source: where its coverage comes from is all that stands behind it

atlas.piece_missing: piece not found at {path} (nor by name in the working directory)

atlas.not_proved: NOT proved on the whole domain. Pieces: {failed}. Uncovered cells: {gaps}; the first: {first}
atlas.proved: on the whole domain the optimum is {relation} {target}: {n} piece(s), covering checked over {cells} cells ({excluded} shown outside the region)
atlas.relative: RELATIVE to {n} cited box(es) certo did not check

commands.q.atlas: the bound holds on each box -- does it hold on the whole domain they are meant to cover?

verify.atlas.boxes: each piece's recorded box is the box its certificate is on
verify.atlas.kind: every piece is a parametric_bound certificate
verify.atlas.program: every piece is about the same program

verify.atlas.detail: {n} piece(s) make one statement, optimum {relation} the claim, for {domain}

engine.param.where_corner: Where: column `{where}` is NEGATIVE at the vertex {point} -- its Bernstein coefficient there, {coef}, is its value ({neg} of {of} coefficients negative). No subdivision shows otherwise at that point: it needs another dual there, a smaller box, or a region.
